I will keep to the cropping pattern I know best: winter wheat followed by summer maize. In Quzhou, that is the safest way for me to use the land for the full year, and it matches the water, weather, and the work rhythm I can still manage at my age. I do not want to spread myself across too many crops, because that means more market risk, more labor, and more chances to make mistakes. Wheat gives me a steady harvest, maize follows it well, and I can use the same land twice.

I will use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed because I want stable emergence, uniform growth, and better yield than old saved seed. I will not chase very high fertilizer rates; I will use enough to hold yield but keep costs under control. For wheat, I will give more water because it needs support through jointing and grain filling. For maize, I will rely partly on summer rain and add irrigation only when the field is dry. I will keep pesticide use limited and timely, only enough to protect the crop through the main disease and insect periods. For tillage, I will use rotary tillage for wheat after maize, and I will use no-tillage for maize after wheat harvest so I can save time and hold moisture. That is the plan I would follow myself this year.
